data.summary: This 3‑week plan starts with a live class on Force and Translational Dynamics to strengthen the student’s weak unit. Week 2 covers the remaining units (Kinematics, Work/Energy, Momentum, Torque, Oscillations, Fluids) with focused practice tasks. Week 3 is a mixed review and timed practice session to consolidate all concepts before the exam.

tasks: Watch the live class 10100 and take detailed notes on free‑body diagrams and Newton’s second law.
Do 15 practice problems on free‑body diagrams and 10 on Newton’s second law, marking each solution against the scoring guide.
Do 20 kinematics problems covering vectors, displacement, and relative motion.
Solve 10 work and energy problems, including conservation of energy scenarios.
Work through 10 linear momentum problems, including impulse and collision cases.
Complete 10 torque and rotational dynamics problems, linking linear and rotational motion.
Practice 10 oscillation problems, calculating frequency and energy.
Answer 10 fluid mechanics questions on pressure and conservation laws.
Take a full-length timed practice test covering all units.
Review incorrect answers and write a brief explanation for each mistake.
Create a summary sheet of key formulas and concepts for quick reference.

data.final_week_advice: Use the last week to simulate exam conditions, focus on time management, and reinforce any lingering weak spots identified during the practice test.
